instruction: A car traveling at a speed of $90 \mathrm{~km/h}$ comes to a stop in $4.0 \mathrm{~s}$ due to friction; calculate the distance the car travels during this time and the work done by friction if the car's mass is $1200 \mathrm{~kg}$.
A 2 kg block slides down a frictionless incline of angle $30^\circ$ from rest; calculate its speed at the bottom of the incline if it descends a vertical height of 5 m.

A 10 kg block is pushed up a 25° incline with an initial speed of 8 m/s; calculate the distance it moves up the incline before coming to rest if the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the incline is 0.2.
A diver leaps from a 3-meter high diving board; calculate the speed of the diver just before hitting the water, ignoring air resistance.
A 2000 kg car accelerates from rest to a speed of 25 m/s in 10 seconds while experiencing a constant friction force of 400 N; calculate the net force exerted on the car during this acceleration.
A cyclist traveling at a speed of 25 m/s applies the brakes and decelerates at a constant rate of 3 m/s²; calculate the distance covered before coming to a complete stop.

A block of mass $5 \mathrm{~kg}$ is sliding down a frictionless incline at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the horizontal; calculate the acceleration of the block and the time it takes to slide down a distance of $2 \mathrm{~m}$.
A 15 kg cart is pushed up a frictionless ramp inclined at 30° with an initial speed of 5 m/s; calculate the maximum height it reaches before coming to a stop.
A 70 kg person is standing at the edge of a 15 m tall cliff and decides to jump off; calculate the speed of the person just before hitting the ground, assuming no air resistance.
A 1500 kg car is traveling at a constant speed of 30 m/s when it suddenly encounters a 5 m high ramp; calculate the speed of the car just after it leaves the ramp, ignoring air resistance.
A 500 g balloon filled with helium rises in the air and reaches a height of 200 m; calculate the work done against gravity in lifting the balloon to this height.
A satellite orbits the Earth at an altitude of 500 km; calculate the satellite's gravitational potential energy if its mass is 1000 kg.

A 60 kg astronaut is floating in space and needs to calculate the amount of fuel required to stop their drift towards a space station that is 100 m away, using a thruster that expels gas at a velocity of 150 m/s; if they aim to stop within 4 seconds, how much mass of fuel must they expel?
A projectile is launched at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with an initial speed of $20 \mathrm{~m/s}$; calculate the maximum height it reaches before falling back to the ground.
A spring with a spring constant of $200 \, \text{N/m}$ is compressed by $0.5 \, \text{m}$; calculate the potential energy stored in the spring when it is compressed.
A 2 kg object is dropped from a height of 45 meters; calculate the speed of the object just before it hits the ground, assuming no air resistance.
A 2 kg block slides down a frictionless ramp inclined at 45° from a height of 10 m; calculate the speed of the block at the bottom of the ramp.

A small block of mass $m = 0.5 \, \text{kg}$ is attached to a spring with spring constant $k = 200 \, \text{N/m}$ and released from a height of $h = 2 \, \text{m}$ above the ground; calculate the maximum compression of the spring when the block collides with it, considering the effects of gravitational potential energy.
Calculate the period of a simple pendulum with a length of 1.5 meters and a small angle approximation for angles less than 15 degrees.

A 2 kg block is attached to a frictionless surface and connected to a spring with a spring constant of 150 N/m; calculate the maximum displacement of the spring from its equilibrium position when the block is pushed with a force of 30 N and released.
A 0.25 kg ball is dropped from a height of 10 m; calculate the speed of the ball just before it hits the ground, assuming air resistance is negligible.
Calculate the work done in compressing a gas at constant pressure of 2 atm from a volume of 10 L to 5 L at a temperature of 300 K.

At a temperature of $350 \mathrm{~K}$ and a pressure of $1.00 \mathrm{~atm}$, calculate the change in enthalpy ($\Delta H$) for the reaction $\mathrm{C(s) + O_2(g) \rightarrow CO_2(g)}$, given that $\Delta H_f^{\circ}(\mathrm{CO_2(g)}) = -393.5 \mathrm{~kJ/mol}$ and $\Delta H_f^{\circ}(\mathrm{C(s)}) = 0$.

A sample of a radioactive isotope has a current activity of 5.0 decay events per minute, and its original activity when it was formed was 50.0 decay events per minute; if the half-life of the isotope is 10 years, how many years old is the sample?
A circular loop of wire with a radius of 10 cm moves with a velocity of 2 m/s perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T; calculate the induced emf in the loop.

A metal rod of length $L = 1.5 \mathrm{~m}$ and cross-sectional area $A = 5.0 \mathrm{~cm}^2$ is subjected to a tensile force of $5000 \mathrm{~N}$; calculate the resulting stress and strain in the rod, given that the Young's modulus for the material is $200 \mathrm{~GPa}$.
Calculate the molar heat capacity of a solid substance after it is heated from 25 °C to 200 °C, resulting in a temperature change of 175 °C and absorbing 500 J of heat in the process.

A cylinder containing an ideal gas is heated from an initial temperature of $T_i = 300 \, \mathrm{K}$ to a final temperature of $T_f = 500 \, \mathrm{K}$ at constant pressure of $1.00 \, \mathrm{atm}$; calculate the change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) given that the molar heat capacity at constant volume is $C_{V,m} = 25 \, \mathrm{J \, mol^{-1} \, K^{-1}}$.

A car of mass $1200 \mathrm{~kg}$ is traveling at a speed of $25 \mathrm{~m/s}$ and suddenly applies brakes with a uniform deceleration of $5 \mathrm{~m/s^2}$; calculate the distance the car travels before coming to a complete stop.
Calculate the gravitational potential energy of a $2.5 \mathrm{~kg}$ mass lifted to a height of $15 \mathrm{~m}$ above the ground.
Calculate the final temperature of 2 kg of water at 20 °C when 0.5 kg of ice at 0 °C is added, assuming no heat loss to the surroundings.

A 2.00 kg block of ice at -10.0 °C is placed in a calorimeter with 0.500 kg of water at 25.0 °C; calculate the final temperature of the system after equilibrium is reached, assuming no heat is lost to the surroundings and the specific heat capacities are 2.09 J/g°C for ice and 4.18 J/g°C for water, and that the heat of fusion of ice is 334 J/g.
A cylindrical tank with a radius of 1 m is filled with water to a height of 4 m; calculate the pressure exerted by the water at the bottom of the tank.

A mass-spring system with a mass of 0.5 kg and a spring constant of 200 N/m is compressed by 0.1 m from its equilibrium position; calculate the potential energy stored in the spring.
